cells.tense: Right now, with the pen in your hand.
cells.verb: seeing what matters before you can explain why
cells.place: in the spot where you decide what gets your attention at all
cells.ask: give one thing you see a shape someone else could pick up — a sentence, a list, a plan — so it stays clear after you've walked away, and things keep making sense around you.
cells.core:
You're picking out what matters before you've worked out why, and it keeps turning out right. You don't have to argue yourself into it and you don't argue anyone else into it either — it lands or it doesn't, and the not-knowing in between doesn't rattle you. Sitting where you sit, that's the whole job, and you're doing it quietly.

What this is free to feed next is form. Seeing clearly is one thing; leaving behind something that holds the shape of what you saw is another. If you wanted to, you could give one thing you know a container — write it down, lay it out, make it something a person could use without you in the room. Not to prove it. Just so it keeps making sense after you've moved on.
cells.sheetLine: You know what matters before you know why, and it holds.

cells.tense: You're living a few steps ahead, in a future you can't actually write yet.
cells.verb: seeing what matters before you can explain why
cells.place: in the spot where you decide what gets your attention at all
cells.ask: name the one thing you actually want from all this and let that choose what gets your attention — then let the rest go unexamined, and the knowing can land again without a fight.
cells.core:
You're gathering more than you can hold so that nothing ahead can catch you unready. Every piece of what you notice gets kept, weighed, turned over, compared with the next piece — and the thing that used to let you see straight through has thickened into something you can't see past. More looking, less seeing. The seat you're in only works when some things are allowed to not matter, and right now nothing is.

What cuts through isn't more sorting. It's wanting something. If you say plainly what you're actually reaching for — not the respectable version, the real one — that pull does the choosing for you. Attention goes where the want points, and everything else can stay unexamined. You'd be surprised how fast the clear seeing comes back once it has a direction to serve.
cells.sheetLine: You're keeping everything so you can't miss anything, and now you can't see.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: seeing what matters before you can explain why
cells.place: in the spot where you decide what gets your attention at all
cells.ask: take one next step without asking anyone whether it's the right one — not the whole road, just the step you can see — and let the seeing come back on its own as you move.
cells.core:
You stopped trusting what you see, and you're still checking with the room that taught you not to. Something registers — this matters, that doesn't — and before it can settle you've already turned to someone else to tell you if it's real. The seeing hasn't gone anywhere. The faith in it did, and you've been borrowing other people's eyes ever since.

The way back isn't to try harder to know. It's to move a little without knowing. Take one step that's only lit as far as the step itself — no map, no second opinion — and see what happens when you're in motion. Moving through what's unclear without forcing it clear is the thing right next to knowing, and when you put weight on it, the knowing starts to fill in behind it. Not all at once. Enough.
cells.sheetLine: You still see it. You just stopped believing yourself.

cells.tense: You're already doing it, and you've set the pen down as if someone else were.
cells.verb: seeing what matters before you can explain why
cells.place: in the spot where you decide what gets your attention at all
cells.ask: the next time a call you made turns out right, give yourself your fair share of it — not luck, not a hunch, yours — and let the knowing you already have sit in the open where you can use it.
cells.core:
You keep landing on the right thing and calling it an accident. The decision that turned out well — you'll say you just happened to go that way, it was a coin toss, who knows. But the same coin keeps coming up the same side, and that isn't chance; that's you, noticing what counts before you had words for it. The seeing is running. Your name isn't on it.

There's a simpler ledger underneath this. When something goes right because you saw it, that's owed to you, the same way a debt is. You wouldn't let someone else take credit for your work; you've just been letting 'luck' take it instead. Try settling the account — one call, one time, counted as yours. Then the knowing stops surprising you and starts being something you can lean on.
cells.sheetLine: You keep getting it right and calling it luck.
